The Land Acquisition Offrcumrdo, ... vs Nalmela Laxmi Bai,
Nizamabad Dist And 4 ... on 11 April, 2025

entities.text: Land Acquisition Offrcumrdo, ... vs Nalmela Laxmi Bai
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Author: Abhinand Kumar Shavili

Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And
 Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Tirumala Devi Eada
 L.A.A.S.No.149 of 2016
Judgment:

(per Hon'ble Smt. Justice Tirumala Devi Eada) This appeal, under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, (for short 'the Act') is preferred by the Land Acquisition Officer, Nizamabad,
aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 02.03.2016 passed in L.A.O.P.No.681 of 2012 by the learned I Additional District Judge at Nizamabad (hereinafter referred to as 'the Reference Court').

entities.text: I Additional District Judge at Nizamabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For convenience and clarity, the parties herein are referred to as they were arrayed before the Reference Court.

3. The facts of the case in brief are that the Revenue Divisional Officer-cum-Land Acquisition Officer has acquired Ac.09-00 guntas of land in survey Nos.349, 350, 351, 352 and 363, situated at Khanapur village of Armoor Mandal for the purpose of house sites to the weaker sections.
The draft notification under Section 4(1) of the Act was published in the Gazette on 26.02.2010.
After conducting due enquiry, the Land Acquisition Officer has awarded Rs.1,02,950/- per acre.

Aggrieved by the said award, the claimants have made an application and the same was referred AKS,J & ETD,J LAAS No.149_2016 under Section 18 of the Act to the Court of I Additional District Judge at Nizamabad.

entities.text: Court of I Additional District Judge at Nizamabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. The case of the claimants is that their land is well irrigated and that they have three borewells in the said land and they used to raise commercial crops and that Armoor village is very nearer to the acquired land, therefore, their lands are suitable for house sites and the rate has to be fixed on square yard basis.

5. The Reference Court has framed the following points for consideration:
"1. Whether the market value fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer is just and reasonable and if not for now much amount the claimants are entitled for?
2. Whether the claimants are entitled for compensation on the acquisition of the open irrigation well and also the bore-wells and if so for how much amount they are The Land Acquisition Offrcumrdo, ... vs Nalmela Laxmi Bai, Nizamabad Dist And 4 ... on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184103270/
1 entitled for compensation on acquiring the open irrigation well and also the bore- wells?"
6.
Before the Reference Court, the claimants got examined PWs 1 to 3 and got marked Exs.A1 and A2.
On behalf of the respondent, RW1 was examined and Ex.B1 was marked.

7. Based on the evidence on record, the Reference Court has awarded a compensation @ Rs.450/-
per square yard for the land acquired after deducting 1/3rd of the acquired land towards development purposes, in addition to the statutory benefits.
AKS,J & ETD,J LAAS No.149_2016
Aggrieved by the said enhancement, the Land Acquisition Officer, has preferred the present appeal.
8. Heard the learned Government Pleader for the appellant and Sri D.Bhaskar Reddy, learned counsel for the respondents.

9. The learned Government Pleader has submitted that the judgment and decree of the reference Court is erroneous and that the reference Court has committed serious error in enhancing the compensation from Rs.1,02,950/- to Rs.21,78,000/- and that the reference Court wrongly relied upon Ex.A2, which is the judgment in O.P.No.1006 of 2004 and ought not to have adopted the time lag principle and that the subject matter of the acquisition under the said OP was for excavation of flood flow canal while the present notification is for the purposes of allotting house sites to weaker sections and therefore, the reference Court should not have awarded a similar amount as that in O.P.No.1006 of 2004.
10.
The learned respondent counsel, on the other hand, has submitted that the reference court has passed a justified order and that there is no need to interfere with the same.

11. Based on the above rival submissions, this Court frames the following points for consideration:
AKS,J & ETD,J LAAS No.149_2016 1.
Whether the claimants are not entitled for enhancement of compensation?
2. Whether the judgment and decree of the reference Court need any interference?

3. To what relief?
12. POINT NO.1:
a) The documents filed by the claimants are under Exs.A1 and A2.
A perusal of the sale deed under Ex.A1 reveals that the sale deed pertains to the year 2002 and that the said document is considered in O.P.No.1006 of 2004.

Under O.P.No.1006 of 2004, the lands acquired pertain to Kisan Nagar village of Balkonda Mandal and the The Land Acquisition Offrcumrdo, ... vs Nalmela Laxmi Bai, Nizamabad Dist And 4 ... on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184103270/
2

entities.text: Land Acquisition Offrcumrdo, ... vs Nalmela Laxmi Bai, Nizamabad Dist And 4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Kisan Nagar village is adjoining to Khanapur village.

Considering the said sale deed which is filed under Ex.A1, the reference Court has enhanced the compensation to Rs.450/-
per square yard, since both the villages are adjoining to each other.

b) A perusal of Ex.B1, the award copy of the Land Acquisition Officer reveals that there were sale transactions in the years 2007- 2008 which are considered by the Land Acquisition Officer and it shows that the rate per acre was around Rs.71,000/- in case of dry lands.

He further observed that the sale amounts are very less as compared with the existing market value as on that date and that the rates of agricultural lands in Khanapur village is ranging from Rs.2 Lakhs to Rs.4 Lakhs depending on the potentiality and AKS,J & ETD,J LAAS No.149_2016 irrigation facilities.
The lands under acquisition are contiguous to Abadi and surrounding lands are being sold on yardage basis.

He further observed that the ryots generally purchase the land at higher prices but get them registered as per the rates available in basic value register and that there is a lot of difference in between the original purchase rate and registered rate.

This observation of RW1 at page No.3 of his award reveals that the rates of the agricultural lands in Khanapur village ranged from Rs.2 Lakhs to Rs.4 Lakhs during the said period and that they have high potentiality and also that the surrounding lands are being sold on yardage basis.
It is elicited from the cross examination of RW1 that the lands under acquisition are adjacent to BT road and that it is suitable for construction of houses.
Thus, it is clearly established through the evidence on record that the land is very much suitable for house sites and that the surrounding lands are sold on yardage basis.

c) The learned counsel for the respondents has relied upon the common judgment passed by this Court in LAAS Nos.382 of 2016 and batch, dated 22.11.2024, wherein a Division Bench of this High Court has dismissed the appeals filed by the Land Acquisition Officer confirming the orders of the reference Court.
In the said case the market value of the acquired land was fixed on yardage basis.

Though, it was agricultural land, the reason assigned for AKS,J & ETD,J LAAS No.149_2016 enhancement of compensation was that the land is fit for house sites and is located in highly developed locality and that the adjacent lands were being sold for house sites on yardage basis.
d) Applying the same principle and in view of the discussion held above, the judgment passed by the reference Court appears to be well justified.
Point No.1 is answered accordingly.

13. POINT NO.2:
In view of the reasoned finding arrived at Point No.1, this Court holds that the judgment and decree of the reference Court do not need any interference.
14.
POINT NO.3:
In the result, the appeal is dismissed upholding the judgment and decree dated 02.03.2016 passed in L.A.O.P.No.681 of 2012 by the learned I Additional District Judge at Nizamabad.
